transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-08
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Ravi (CTO, Novatek), Elena (Head of ML), Dave (Infra), Sofia (Procurement)

Summary (auto): POC scoping call to define capacity sizing and autoscale approach for a 3-week proof-of-concept. Discussed reserved GPUs, burst strategy for traffic spikes, fallback policies, success criteria (latency, throughput, cost), and benchmark plan. Next steps: Redwood to send pricing and benchmark plan; Novatek to provide workload profile and security/RFC items.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick introductions then we'll jump into the POC goals.
[00:12] Ravi: Yeah hi, Ravi from Novatek, CTO. We're looking to validate inference for our assistant product, need to see cost and latency at scale.
[00:18] Elena: Elena here, ML lead. we'll own the test prompts and evals, have some preference for a 16k-context model but can test smaller first.
[00:26] Samir: Samir, SE at Redwood, I will run the benchmark with you and map to capacity.
[00:30] Dave: Dave, infra. i'll surface networking constraints, we run in GCP us-west2 with strict egress controls.
[00:36] Sofia: Sofia, procurement, I'll coordinate contracts.

[01:00] Maya: Goal for today is to align success criteria, expected qps, typical sequence lengths, and agree on reserved GPU sizing + burst/fallback approach. Also timelines for a 2-3 week POC.

[01:20] Ravi: High level targets: we want p99 latency under 350ms for user-facing LLM completions at peak, and cost no worse than our current hosted vendor — roughly $0.20 per 1k tokens target, but that's flexible. Our traffic shape: baseline 30 qps, peak 120 qps for 20-30 mins during rolling events.

[01:50] Samir: ok good. can you share distribution for seq length? that's the big factor for GPU throughput.

[02:05] Elena: Most requests are short: 70% under 256 tokens, 25% around 512, and 5% long chains up to 8k when users request context summarization. We can sample payloads.

[02:30] Samir: That's helpful. For the POC we recommend reserving a small pool to guarantee baseline — e.g., 2 x A10-like GPUs for baseline and allow burst to a larger pool for spikes. The exact instance type depends on model choice and quantization.

[02:55] Dave: We need to clarify reserved vs. dedicated terms. reserved means we're committing for the POC duration, right? we don't want surprises on billing if burst happens.

[03:08] Maya: Yes reserved = guaranteed capacity for the POC period. billing can be set to a timeboxed reservation. Burst is additional capacity that Redwood can pull from a shared pool; we'll include a burst cap and rate limit to prevent runaway costs. We'll propose pricing options in the quote.

[03:30] Elena: On model family, we prefer open Llama-like models, and quantization is fine if it doesn't break quality. We need an A/B comparison for quantized vs fp16 to ensure negligible quality delta.

[03:48] Samir: Understood. For throughput, with 2x A10-class we can expect around 40-60 qps for short requests at seq len 256 depending on batching. For your peaks you'll need burst to handle 120 qps. We can size burst to an additional 4 GPUs to reach target headroom.

[04:15] Ravi: Can you explain fallback policies? If burst capacity is exhausted, what happens?

[04:25] Samir: Two-tier fallback we typically use: first fallback to a cheaper or smaller model variant (lower tokens per second but lower cost), second fallback is rate-limited queuing with a grace degrade message. Optionally you can configure region fallback to another cluster. For the POC we recommend model-variant fallback + short queueing (30s) before returning an ETA.

[04:55] Dave: Region fallback may be tricky for us because of data residency and VPC peering. we prefer model-variant fallback.

[05:05] Maya: Noted. We'll propose a default policy: reserved pool -> burst pool -> model-variant fallback -> queue. We'll include timeouts and circuit-breakers.

[05:22] Elena: For benchmarks, we want to test: 1) steady-state 30 qps for 60 minutes, 2) synthetic spike 120 qps for 30 minutes, 3) long-context throughput with seq len 8k for 15 minutes. Also quality checks comparing quantized vs fp16 on 200 prompt set.

[05:45] Samir: Good. We'll run those and capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, GPU util, tokens/sec, and cost per token. We usually instrument with per-request traces. We'll also run KV cache warm/cold scenarios.

[06:08] Ravi: How do you handle prefix caching? for our summarization flows we have many repeated system prompts.

[06:18] Samir: Redwood supports prefix/KV caching; you can pin common prefixes and get big wins for long sequences. For the POC we'll enable prefix cache and measure delta. Some models depend on decoder-only caching — we'll confirm compatibility with the model weights you pick.

[06:38] Elena: One constraint: we can't expose raw user data to shared pools, so any burst capacity must be either into encrypted transit or run on dedicated bursts. Is that possible?

[06:50] Maya: For POCs we can either restrict burst to dedicated machines or ensure encrypted networking + tenancy controls. There's a tradeoff in cost. We'll call out both options in the quote: dedicated burst (higher cost) vs shared burst with strict encryption and egress controls.

[07:10] Dave: We'll need KMS integration and audit logs for any infra touching PII. Can you provide SOC2 logs?

[07:18] Maya: Yes we will share SOC2 and KMS integration notes. action item for us to attach security pack.

[07:28] Sofia: On contracting, procurement needs an MSA addendum for reserved capacity and a clear window for cancellation post-POC.

[07:36] Maya: We'll draft a POC addendum and include cancellation terms and a timebox for the reserved term.

[07:50] Samir: Back to sizing: given your mix, recommended POC config: baseline 2 x A10-class (reserved), burst up to +4 GPUs (either shared or dedicated), model-variant fallback to a smaller 30B quantized model, and circuit breaker at 200 qps. This should keep p99 under 350ms for short requests.

[08:18] Elena: Sounds reasonable. For the long-context 8k tests we expect lower qps; what's the expected throughput?

[08:28] Samir: For 8k context, throughput drops significantly — maybe ~2-5 qps per GPU depending on model. We'll document expected numbers in the benchmark plan.

[08:38] Ravi: Timelines: we want to start POC next week and run 2-3 weeks. Is that feasible?

[08:46] Maya: If we get your traffic samples and sign the POC addendum by Friday (2026-04-10), we can provision reserved GPUs and start baseline tests early next week. Full POC run across scenarios in 2 weeks after that.

[09:02] Dave: Provisioning for reserved GPUs — how long does that take?

[09:08] Samir: Usually 24-48 hours once capacity approved; dedicated bursts may take longer if we need to carve capacity in a region. We'll call out lead times in the quote.

[09:20] Elena: On metrics and dashboards, we want token-level cost, per-route latency, and model quality regression alerts.

[09:29] Maya: Redwood Console supports all of those. We'll enable per-route dashboards and set up a shared project for you.

[09:38] Ravi: One more thing: can you run a preliminary test with a 30-minute spike to prove autoscale behavior and billing metering?

[09:46] Samir: Yes we'll schedule a 30-minute spike test during the baseline benchmark window. We'll capture autoscale latency (time to scale up) and any dropped requests.

[09:58] Maya: Ok let's recap next steps. Redwood action items: pricing + reserved/burst quote, security pack + SOC2, benchmark plan and test window proposals. Novatek action items: share request samples, seq length distribution, confirm legal points for POC addendum.

[10:20] Sofia: Procurement will review the POC addendum. expect feedback within 3 business days.

[10:28] Ravi: We'll aim to have samples and qps targets to you by Monday.

[10:35] Maya: Great. Samir, anything to add?

[10:38] Samir: I'll draft the benchmark scripts, include warm/cold KV cache, quantized vs fp16 runs, and send invites for the test run.

[10:46] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and the quote.

[11:00] End of call.

Notes on transcription quality: there are some mis-heard proper nouns and occasional speaker attribution inaccuracies. The transcript retains filler words and minor stutters to preserve authenticity.

References mentioned: Benchmark plan (link to be shared), SOC2 whitepaper (Redwood security pack), Reserved capacity quote (attached in follow-up).
